diagnosis: Work output is materially unstable on the same fixed Task/Event input: predicted Work count changes 4 -> 5 -> 6 and Work F1 ranges 0.7230-0.8450.
The instability is therefore attributable to the Task-to-Work LLM stage, not Event or Task variation in this repeat test.

In the last run, the main false-negative block is the new-car project: Tasks from the first and second new-car task groups are grouped together, but the third new-car task group is split away, causing many missing within-Work pairs.

The battery-warranty cross-thread Work does not appear in the last-run false-negative pairs, indicating that cross-thread inference can succeed; the failure is not a blanket inability to merge across threads.
A second last-run split occurs inside the customer-complaint Work, where the first Task is separated from the other Tasks.
False-positive Work pairs involving UNMAPPED predicted Tasks are partly downstream of Task over-splitting/alignment error, so they should not be interpreted as pure Work-semantic errors.

No prompt change is justified from this case alone. Next step is repeated fixed-upstream regression across multiple global cases and/or a consensus/deterministic stabilization strategy if the same Work variance persists.
